# Recreation Prompt

Recreate Neon Loop Rush as a portrait-first browser canvas runner. Preserve the mechanics of a fixed-left avatar that jumps on tap, is pulled down by gravity, clears scrolling obstacles, earns +10 rings for each clean pass, fills a distance progress bar, fails on rectangle collision, and wins by crossing a finish loop gate. Present the game as an original Sonic-inspired neon arcade speedway: a blue spiky speedster mascot named Volt races through loop-heavy rails, checkered gates, ring halos, magenta hazards, cyan speed lines, and rebellious cartoon UI. Keep controls touch-friendly, HUD readable, and all primary runtime code inline in index.html.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint — Source Truth and Rebuild Target

## Source game truth
The preserved source is an inline canvas endless/finite runner titled Sky Courier Rush. It has menu, route select, character select, settings, HUD, pause, fail, and victory screens. The active loop is a side-scrolling platform runner: a fixed-left avatar jumps on tap, gravity returns it to the ground, obstacles spawn from the right, passing obstacles adds score, colliding with obstacles fails, and reaching a distance goal spawns a finish gate for victory.

## Protected mechanics
- Pointer/tap on the gameplay canvas triggers a single jump only while grounded.
- Gravity, jump impulse, fixed ground line, and grounded state determine movement.
- Obstacles scroll left at speed that increases with distance.
- Collision is rectangle overlap with padding.
- Score increases by 10 when obstacles are passed.
- Distance drives progress bar and finish gate/victory.
- Pause, resume, quit, restart, next-loop, route selection, and sound toggle remain available.

## Safe transformation surfaces
Title, copy, HUD labels, route names, colors, canvas drawing, actor/hazard silhouettes, background, particles, panels, typography, synth audio tones, and progression names are safe to transform. The old stock/image-backed sky presentation is not mechanic-critical.

## Rebuild target
Create a self-contained portrait-first game named Neon Loop Rush. It preserves the runner mechanics while making the world a Sonic-inspired original neon speedway with loop arcs, ring scoring, kinetic set pieces, and an original blue speedster focal identity.
